newsitem.title: USA: Oroville, Calif., taps bond reserve - officials.
newsitem.headline: Oroville, Calif., taps bond reserve - officials.

text.p: Oroville, Calif.,'s public finance authority tapped into the reserve of a 1992 revenue bond issue in order to pay investors in full on March 15, but warned it may not have the money to pay bondholders in 1998, city officials said on Friday.
To pay holders of the revenue bonds, the reserve funds were drawn upon on March 15 in the amount of $47,294. Similar draws were made on the reserve funds in 1996.
The city said the reserve funds for the Series 1992 and 1992B bonds now hold a total of $147,403. The total debt service on the revenue bonds due on September 15 is $173,586.

The Oroville Public Financing Authority, formed by the city and the city's redevelopment agency, said it believes with reserve funds and other revenues it will be able to cover the debt service on the revenue bonds on September 15.

"However, if the foreclosure actions ... are not concluded by March 15, 1998 and sufficient assessment installments and judgment amounts are not received in a timely fashion, there may be insufficient funds available to make full payment of debt service on the revenue bonds on March 15, 1998," the authority said in a statement. As of June 30, 1996, an estimated $3.21 million of the revenue bonds were outstanding.
